implementation: The opt-in q8192 route buckets an existing compact candidate list by its existing expert ID. One device count memset, histogram, prefix and scatter produce a permutation in separately owned storage. The replay grid consumes the reordered indices with its original floating-point operands, candidate predicate, K16 accumulation and activation. The list remains in the original routed stream with no host count read. The full window owns16780292 additional bytes. Original and ordered lists must be separate allocations; the existing producer guarantees count within capacity and expert IDs in0..255. Partition replay and parallel routed gate are incompatible and rejected. Default disabled.
ownership_validation: Host harnesses exercise the real owner, actual launch arguments and every fallible submission, all compaction allocation failures for two window sizes with disabled/enabled ordering, repeated cleanup and drain failure preventing free. The owner harness uses a CPU stable-sort stand-in to check scheduling and exact candidate/math preservation; it does not emulate GPU atomics. The independent native suite executes the actual HIP histogram, prefix and scatter.
numerical_scope: Seventy-two independent native cases check empty, single, partial and full counts at256,4096,4194304 capacities,512/2048 columns and one-expert, distributed and strongly skewed expert populations. Each output must be the exact input permutation, monotonically bucketed by expert, with every histogram, offset and cursor verified, unused slots and guards unchanged and original inputs immutable. Four integrated routed cases compare original local replay, existing prepared variants, existing staged replay and expert-ordered staged replay by raw floating-point bits and BF16 activation, including unsupported K16 fallback. Separate existing staged-only cases and norm scans also pass. These generated tests are not GB10 model inference.
timing_scope: Integrated routed intervals include original correction dispatch, optional norm/operand preparation, sorting when enabled and stream completion. These are single diagnostic component intervals, not retained product measurements. Allocation, transfers, resets and verification are outside the intervals. Real q8192 product measurement is required.
decision: Native permutation, arithmetic and ownership checks pass. Proceed to the same-DLL real q8192/out512 comparison with the full GB10 boundary. No release or product performance qualification follows from these component tests.
